attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The finite matrix derivation is valid, but it does not compute the actual Yang-Mills boundary hairpin defect B or the realized collar matrix N. The missing analytic input is a boundary OPE or multiscale estimate for three reflected Wilson hairpins that proves N=B\circ M with zero additive contact and then controls the quotient determinant.
steps: Start with fixed collar observables F_i^\delta. Regulated reflection positivity gives Q_{a,L}\ge0; RG convergence in the reflected-probe topology gives a positive collar-limit Gram matrix N for each finite family.
Collapse the collar. If diagonal trace continuity is valid and additive boundary contacts vanish, the only remaining defect in a reflected Wilson product is multiplicative: N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}.
The same-theory target is not N and not a boundary-renormalized replacement; it is M=B^{[-1]}\circ N on the locked Wilson algebra.
For two observables, positivity of M gives the known threshold |n_{12}|/|b_{12}|\le1, so pairwise tests only control 2 by 2 minors.
For three observables, normalize M to diagonal one. The determinant expands exactly as 1-|q_{12}|^2-|q_{23}|^2-|q_{13}|^2+2 Re(q_{12}q_{23}\overline{q_{13}}).

Writing q_{ij}=n_{ij}/b_{ij} isolates the new invariant: the determinant depends on the phase difference between the collar triangle n_{12}n_{23}\overline{n_{13}} and the boundary defect triangle b_{12}b_{23}\overline{b_{13}}.

If all quotient cycle phases vanish on a finite family, a diagonal unitary removes the phases and the problem reduces to modulus quotient positivity. If a triangle phase remains, it is the first phase-sensitive falsifier candidate.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The argument proves an exact conditional detector for finite matrices. It does not prove that the RG cutoff-removal topology controls the required triple Wilson collar limits, nor that the boundary defect has trivial cycle phase or positive modulus quotient on a dense Wilson core.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Three-Hairpin Schur-Preimage Phase Test

assumptions: Diagonal trace continuity is already valid: N_{ii}=B_{ii}M_{ii} with finite positive diagonal entries and no hidden diagonal boundary loss.
Additive contact terms vanish or have been independently proved zero on this triple; otherwise the multiplicative quotient model is not valid.
The boundary defect matrix B is Hermitian with nonzero tested entries and is computed from the same reflected hairpin geometry that appears in the collar collapse.
N is a realized collar-limit OS Gram matrix for actual Yang-Mills Wilson observables, not an arbitrary positive matrix inserted for a universal Schur-multiplier argument.
definitions: source object: a finite locked gauge-invariant Wilson collar family F_i^\delta supported in t>\delta, with regulated reflection-positive Schwinger matrices converging to a positive collar-limit OS matrix N.
target object: the intended continuum OS matrix M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) on the same Wilson observables after the collar is collapsed to the reflection plane.

controlled interface: the boundary OPE comparison map N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij} and hence M=B^{[-1]}\circ N, tested on every realized finite Wilson OS matrix rather than on the full cone of all positive matrices.

same-theory condition: the observables F_i^\delta converge to the locked F_i without changing Wilson-loop renormalization, adding a boundary counterterm, enlarging the algebra, or replacing M by a boundary-renormalized theory.

equations.label: multiplicative boundary quotient
equations.valid_when: The collar collapse has no additive contact term, B_{ij}\neq0 on the tested entries, and the same locked Wilson observable is used before and after the limit.

equations.label: normalized three by three OS determinant
equations.valid_when: The diagonal entries of M are positive and \widehat M_{ij}=q_{ij}=M_{ij}/\sqrt{M_{ii}M_{jj}} is the normalized intended OS matrix for three observables.

equations.label: triangle phase obstruction
equations.valid_when: The normalized collar entries n_{ij} and boundary entries b_{ij} are nonzero; then \det\widehat M=1-\sum r_{ij}^2+2r_{12}r_{23}r_{13}\cos\Phi.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find three locked reflected Wilson hairpins for which |n_{ij}|\le |b_{ij}| for all pairs, but 1-\sum r_{ij}^2+2r_{12}r_{23}r_{13}\cos\Phi<0. That would be a valid same-theory falsifier even though all two-observable tests pass.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma makes the first non-pairwise same-theory obstruction finite and computable: closed-cone positivity gives N\ge0, but the intended target requires the Hadamard preimage B^{[-1]}\circ N\ge0 on realized Wilson triples.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a locked triple of reflected Wilson collar observables, assume fixed-collar OS positivity has passed to a positive collar-limit matrix N and collar collapse has only a multiplicative boundary hairpin defect B, with additive contacts already ruled out. Then same-theory OS positivity for the intended continuum boundary matrix M is equivalent, for this triple, to positivity of the Hadamard quotient M=B^{[-1]}\circ N. After normalization, the first phase-sensitive obstruction is the determinant inequality 1-r_{12}^2-r_{23}^2-r_{13}^2+2r_{12}r_{23}r_{13}\cos(\Phi_N-\Phi_B)\ge0. Thus a realized Wilson triple with pairwise valid thresholds but negative triangle determinant is a concrete falsifier of the bridge.

assumptions: The tested quotient graph is connected and all entries used in cycle tests are nonzero; zero boundary entries require a separate singular-defect analysis.
Cycle phase triviality is checked on all cycles of the realized finite family, not merely on one chosen triangle unless the family has three vertices.
The modulus quotient R is tested on the realized Wilson cone; universal positivity on all matrices is stronger than needed and should not be assumed.
definitions: cycle phase: for a cycle C=(i_1,...,i_k,i_1), the invariant holonomy \prod_\ell q_{i_\ell i_{\ell+1}}/|q_{i_\ell i_{\ell+1}}|.
modulus quotient: the Hermitian matrix R with R_{ii}=1 and R_{ij}=|n_{ij}|/|b_{ij}| for i\ne j.
phase coboundary: a representation q_{ij}=u_i\overline{u_j}R_{ij} with |u_i|=1, so the phase changes only the basis vectors in the OS pre-Hilbert space.

equations.label: phase holonomy criterion
equations.valid_when: The quotient graph is connected and all edge entries q_{ij} on the graph are nonzero.

equations.label: unitary reduction to modulus quotient
equations.valid_when: The phase holonomy criterion holds; then \widehat M\ge0 if and only if R\ge0 for the tested finite family.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A single realized cycle with nontrivial quotient holonomy, especially a three-hairpin triangle, prevents diagonal phase removal and must be tested by the determinant criterion.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives a promotion route: prove boundary and collar OPE phases have matching cycle holonomy, then the phase falsifier disappears and the remaining task is a modulus PSD estimate.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For any finite locked Wilson family with nonzero quotient entries q_{ij}=n_{ij}/b_{ij}, if every cycle phase of q is trivial, then the quotient phase is a diagonal unitary coboundary. In that case the phase obstruction can be removed by a harmless unitary congruence, and same-theory OS positivity reduces to positivity of the real modulus quotient matrix R_{ij}=|n_{ij}|/|b_{ij}| on the realized Wilson family.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from the OS-preserving RG route if a valid realized three-hairpin computation gives det(B^{[-1]}\circ N)<0 or if the boundary quotient is singular with B_{ij}=0 and N_{ij}\ne0.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the bridge if one proves, on a dense locked Wilson core, zero additive contacts, multiplicative anomaly N=B\circ M, quotient cycle phases that are diagonal coboundaries, and positive modulus quotient matrices for all finite realized families.
control_decision.reason: The branch made substantive progress: it replaced a vague nonrank-one boundary-Gram warning with an exact three-observable determinant and a cycle-phase coboundary criterion. This is a narrower and more testable bridge than the previous pairwise threshold.

dependency_updates.description: Split into a formal closed-cone passage producing positive collar-limit matrices N and a separate same-theory Hadamard-preimage condition M=B^{[-1]}\circ N for boundary-collapsed Wilson observables.
The algebra must include locked Wilson collar triples and their boundary collapses, because pairwise tests are insufficient for OS positivity after a boundary defect.
The topology must converge finite reflected Wilson matrices and preserve enough boundary OPE data to define N, B, and the quotient determinant.

A new dependency: compute or bound the multiplicative boundary Gram factor B and prove B^{[-1]}\circ N is positive on all realized finite Wilson families, with the first nontrivial test at three observables.

falsifiers: A realized three-hairpin Wilson family with |n_{ij}|\le |b_{ij}| for every pair but det(B^{[-1]}\circ N)<0 is the sharp phase falsifier for this cycle.
A boundary entry B_{ij}=0 with N_{ij}\ne0 makes the Hadamard preimage singular and invalidates the same-theory quotient map.
A nonzero additive boundary contact that is not forced to vanish by diagonal trace continuity breaks the multiplicative anomaly model before the phase test is even reached.
A quotient cycle phase that cannot be written as a diagonal unitary coboundary gives a valid obstruction unless the realized modulus matrix still keeps every finite determinant nonnegative.

If the locked Wilson algebra cannot realize triples rich enough to test the boundary covariance, then nontrivial B is not yet a falsifier; the branch would need a stronger density theorem rather than a determinant example.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 201 sharpened the obstruction from pairwise damping to finite quotient holonomy. The closed-cone step is still valid for collar matrices N, but same-theory OS positivity depends on whether the Hadamard preimage B^{[-1]}\circ N is positive on realized Wilson families. The first genuinely new falsifier is a three-hairpin triangle whose quotient phase makes the normalized determinant negative. Conversely, if quotient phases are cycle-trivial, they are removable by diagonal unitary congruence, so the next proof route separates into phase-coboundary control plus modulus quotient positivity.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the leading boundary OPE for three reflected Wilson hairpins with a common reflection-plane footprint. Extract B_{12}, B_{23}, B_{13} and the collar triangle N_{12}N_{23}\overline{N_{13}}, then evaluate the normalized determinant of B^{[-1]}\circ N to see whether the first phase-sensitive falsifier is realized.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
